Sweet Potato Casserole with Pecan Topping

Served at: Thanksgiving Day (United States)

Serves 8-10Prep 25 minCook 50 min

Sweet Potato Casserole is a beloved staple on many American Thanksgiving tables, offering a delightful balance of sweet and savory flavors. Often served alongside turkey and other traditional dishes, its creamy texture and crunchy pecan topping make it a comforting and festive addition to the holiday feast.

Ingredients

  • 4 lbs (1.8 kg) sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) cubes
  • 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, melted, plus more for greasing
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) whole milk or half-and-half
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) packed light brown sugar
  • 2 large eggs, lightly beaten
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1 cup (100 g) chopped pecans
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) packed light brown sugar
  • 1/3 cup (40 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/4 cup (57 g) unsalted butter, melted

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Lightly grease a 9x13 inch (23x33 cm) baking dish with butter.
  2. Place the peeled and cubed sweet potatoes in a large pot and cover with cold water. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat and cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
  3. Drain the sweet potatoes thoroughly and return them to the pot. Mash them with a potato masher or an electric mixer until smooth.
  4. Add the 1/2 cup (113 g) melted butter, milk, granulated sugar, 1/4 cup (50 g) brown sugar, eggs, vanilla extract, and salt to the mashed sweet potatoes. Mix well until everything is fully combined and smooth.
  5. Pour the sweet potato mixture into the prepared baking dish and spread evenly.
  6. In a medium bowl, combine the chopped pecans, 1/2 cup (100 g) brown sugar, and flour for the topping. Pour the 1/4 cup (57 g) melted butter over the mixture and stir with a fork until crumbly and well combined.
  7. Evenly sprinkle the pecan topping over the sweet potato mixture in the baking dish.
  8. Bake for 30 minutes, then loosely tent with foil to prevent the topping from over-browning, and continue baking for another 15-20 minutes, or until the casserole is heated through and the topping is golden brown and bubbly.
  9. Remove from the oven and let rest for 5-10 minutes before serving.

Tips

  • For a make-ahead option, prepare the sweet potato mixture and topping separately, then assemble and bake on Thanksgiving Day.
  • If you prefer a sweeter casserole, you can increase the amount of granulated sugar in the sweet potato base by 1/4 cup (50 g).
  • For a classic marshmallow topping variation, omit the pecan topping and instead, during the last 10-15 minutes of baking, cover the casserole with 4-5 cups (200-250 g) of mini marshmallows and bake until golden brown and puffed.
